p1_b3.ocr: The fifth row for Phragmites (E) shows 2.38 ± 0.30 C for N, 0.34 ± 0.05 B for P, 0.30 ± 0.01 C for Phenolics, 24.85 ± 1.09 A for Cellulose, 6.64 ± 0.57 A for Lignin, and 237.69 ± 38.57 A for Toughness. The second table contains Test Number, Common name, Brief description, Region examined, Protein, and Gene. For Test Number 1, the common name is pN/pS, with a brief description of nonsynonymous vs synonymous differences within Kenyan bees, examined in Protein-coding, with Protein Venom allergen Api m 6 and Gene GB45615. Test Number 2 has no common name, describing nonsynonymous differences between Kenyan and European Apis mellifera, also in Protein-coding, with Protein FMRFamide receptor and Gene GB51916. Test Number 3, labeled McDonald- Kreitman test, details nonsynonymous differences between Kenyan bees and Apis florea, in Protein-coding with Protein NADH dehydrogenase (ubiquinone) 1 beta subcomplex and Gene GB51330. Test Number 4 is ROH, indicating runs of homozygosity, under Genome-wide, with Protein FoxO and Gene GB48301. Test Number 5, FST, addresses differences between two populations of Kenyan bees, also Genome-wide, with Protein Neuroligin-3 and Gene GB42603. Test Number 6, Tajima’s D, discusses allele frequency spectrum, in Genome-wide, with Proteins RpA70, ZFYVE26 and Genes GB44421, GB44416.
